newsitem.title: UK: NWE naphtha rallies as arbitrage talk circulates.
newsitem.headline: NWE naphtha rallies as arbitrage talk circulates.

text.p: NWE naphtha rallied on Tuesday after crude surged and speculation blossomed that the arbitrage may be open to the U.S. and attracting cargoes, traders and brokers said.
A roughly 25,000 tonne Egyptian cargo was sold on Tuesday at $226 cif basis Rotterdam for delivery by the end of the month, they said.

They disagreed over whether the arbitrage to the U.S. was fully open but there appeared to be some interest in transatlantic dealings. A 35,000 tonne Greek cargo was believed to have been fixed in the last few days, but this could not be confirmed, they said.
But the NWE market still looked fairly well balanced for the second half of the month.
"Crude oil is driving this market for now and gas oil is driving crude," said a Scandinavian trader. "So it looks like the cold weather is driving the market."
"It's totally crude dependent," the trader said. "I still think the market is well balanced."
Dec swaps gained $3 to $220/$221 with January at $214/$215.25 and Feb at $208.50/$209.50.
Results of the Egyptian tender for 1997 were expected this week with speculation that they will come in at a premium to mean fob Med prices by $6.50 to slightly more than $7, traders said.
Traders were also watching the weather at Algeria's Skikda for any delays in loadings. The port is open.
